question: Why did the error rate go up on 20 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: New deployment of catalog v4.20 to us-east caused the error rate to rise in eu-west.
why_chain: Deployed catalog v4.20 to us-east (record R014) caused the error rate to rise in eu-west (record E1).
The error rate in eu-west increased from 0.53% to 1.14% (record E1).
The error rate in eu-west was the only segment that changed (record E2).

contributing_factors.description: The increase in error rate is not due to a change in request volume or latency.
why_chain: The error rate in eu-west increased from 0.53% to 1.14% (record E1).
The request volume in eu-west stayed about the same (record E3).
The p95 latency in eu-west stayed about the same (record E4).

ruled_out.hypothesis: The typo on the help page caused the error rate to rise.
ruled_out.reason: Customer reports a typo on the help page (record R013) is not related to the error rate increase in eu-west (record E1).

ruled_out.hypothesis: The customer asking how to download an invoice caused the error rate to rise.
ruled_out.reason: Customer asks how to download an invoice (record R011) is not related to the error rate increase in eu-west (record E1).

ruled_out.hypothesis: The routine release of checkout v3.20 to ap-south caused the error rate to rise in eu-west.
ruled_out.reason: Routine release of checkout v3.20 to ap-south (record R012) is not related to the error rate increase in eu-west (record E1).

evidence.summary: Error rate for service checkout in region eu-west rose from 0.53% to 1.14% (+115%), with a change point at 2026-03-20T09:35:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service checkout in region eu-west: 1 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.12).
At the same time, request volume for service checkout in region eu-west stayed about the same (280 per 5 min before, 348 per 5 min after, +25%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service checkout in region eu-west stayed about the same (222 ms before, 223 ms after, +0%).
Deployed catalog v4.20 to us-east (catalog, us-east; 1 min before the change; record R014; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
Customer reports a typo on the help page. (catalog, us-east; 91 min before the change; record R013; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
Deployed checkout v3.20 to ap-south (routine release) (checkout, ap-south; 278 min before the change; record R012; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)
Customer asks how to download an invoice. (auth, us-east; 340 min before the change; record R011; fit: different service/region, so unlikely to be the cause)

reasons: ✓ A change event (deploys) lines up in time (1 min before the change).
✗ It concerns a different service/region than the one that changed.
✗ No logs or alerts from the affected segment confirm the problem.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.
missing_data: Change records for the affected service/region
Error logs or traces from the affected segment after the change

actions.action: Roll back the catalog v4.20 deployment to us-east.
Monitor the error rate in eu-west for the next 24 hours and take further action if the error rate continues to rise.
Review the deployment process for catalog v4.20 to ensure it does not cause similar issues in the future.
